source_text: Ταῦτα δὴ καὶ τὰ τούτοις ἀνάλογον ἀπόῤῥητα ἐπιστάμενοι Μωϋσῆς καὶ οἱ προφῆται ἀπαγορεύουσιν „ὄνομα θεῶν ἑτέρων“ ὀνομάζειν ἐν στόματι, μελετήσαντι τῷ ἐπὶ πᾶσι μόνῳ εὔχεσθαι θεῷ, καὶ ἀναμνημονεύειν ἐν καρδίᾳ, διδασκομένῃ καθαρεύειν ἀπὸ πάσης ματαιότητος νοημάτων καὶ λέξεων. καὶ διὰ τὰ τοιαῦτα πᾶσαν αἰκίαν ὑπομένειν μᾶλλον αἱρούμεθα ἢ τὸν Δία ὁμολογῆσαι θεόν. οὐ γὰρ τὸν αὐτὸν εἶναι ὑπολαμβάνομεν Δία καὶ Σαβαὼθ, ἀλλ᾿ οὐδ᾿ ὅλως θεῖόν τι τὸν Δία, δαίμονα δέ τινα χαίρειν οὕτως ὀνομαζόμενον, οὐ φίλον ἀνθρώποις οὐδὲ τῷ ἀληθινῷ θεῷ. κἂν Αἰγύπτιοι δὲ τὸν Ἀμοῦν ἡμῖν προτείνωσιν κόλασιν ἀπειλοῦντες, τεθνηξόμεθα μᾶλλον ἢ τὸν Ἀμοῦν ἀναγορεύσομεν θεὸν, παραλαμβανόμενον ὡς εἰκὸς ἔν τισιν Αἰγυπτίαις καλούσαις τὸν δαίμονα τοῦτον ἐπῳδαῖς. λεγέτωσαν δὲ καὶ Σκύθαι τὸν Παπαῖον θεὸν εἶναι τὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν· ἀλλ᾿ ἡμεῖς οὐ πεισόμεθα. τιθέντες μὲν τὸν ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεὸν. ὡς δὲ φίλον τῷ λαχόντι τὴν Σκυθῶν ἐρημίαν καὶ τὸ ἔθνος αὐτῶν καὶ τὴν διάλεκτον οὐκ ὀνομάζοντες τὸν θεὸν ὡς κυρίῳ ὀνόματι τῷ Παπαῖον. Σκυθιστὶ γὰρ τὸ προσηγορικὸν τὸν θεὸν καὶ Αἰγυπτιστὶ καὶ πάσῃ διαλέκτῳ, ᾗ ἕκαστος ἐντέθραπται. ὀνομάζων οὐχ ἁμαρτήσεται.
thought_title: Why Christians will not call God Zeus
pass_a_gloss: Knowing these and the secret things analogous to them, Moses and the prophets forbid to name 'name of other gods' in a mouth that has practised to pray to the God over all alone, and to make mention in a heart being taught to be pure from all vanity of thoughts and words. And because of such things we choose to endure every outrage/torture rather than confess Zeus God. For we do not suppose Zeus and Sabaoth to be the same, but not at all anything divine the Zeus, but some demon rejoicing to be so named, not friend to men nor to the true God. And if Egyptians hold out Amoun to us threatening punishment, we shall die rather than proclaim Amoun god, taken up as is likely in some Egyptian incantations calling this demon. And let Scythians say Papaios to be the God over all; but we shall not be persuaded; positing indeed the God over all, but not naming God, as is dear to the one who obtained by lot the wilderness of the Scythians and their nation and language, with Papaios as proper name. For naming God in Scythian by the common noun, and in Egyptian, and in every language in which each was brought up, he will not sin.

pass_b_english: It is because they knew these secret things, and others like them, that Moses and the prophets forbid anyone to speak “the name of other gods” (Exodus 23:13) with a mouth that has learned to pray only to the God over all, or to call them to mind in a heart taught to keep itself pure from all vanity of thoughts and words. And for such reasons we choose to endure every kind of torture rather than confess that Zeus is a god. For we do not suppose that Zeus and Sabaoth are the same; indeed, we do not suppose Zeus to be anything divine at all, but some demon who delights in being called by that name, and who is no friend either to men or to the true God.

And if the Egyptians hold Amoun out to us and threaten us with punishment, we shall die rather than proclaim Amoun a god, a name that is probably used in certain Egyptian incantations that call upon this demon. Let the Scythians, too, say that Papaeus is the God over all; but we shall not be persuaded. We do hold that there is a God over all; but we do not name God by Papaeus as a proper name, as pleases the one who was allotted the Scythian wilderness, together with their nation and their language. For whoever names God by the common word for God, in Scythian or in Egyptian or in any language in which he was brought up, will not sin.
notes: 'The name of other gods' matches LXX Exodus 23:13 (ὄνομα θεῶν ἑτέρων οὐκ ἀναμνησθήσεσθε, οὐδὲ μὴ ἀκουσθῇ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος ὑμῶν), which supplies both 'mouth' and 'call to mind'. Origen says 'Moses and the prophets'; possible further echoes, not cited inline: Joshua 23:7, Psalm 16:4 (LXX 15:4, 'nor will I take their names upon my lips'), Hosea 2:17. 'The one who was allotted the Scythian wilderness' alludes to Origen's view that nations were allotted to angelic powers (cf. LXX Deuteronomy 32:8); not a quotation, so not cited inline. The source punctuation (full stops after θεόν and Παπαῖον, and after ἐντέθραπται) is treated as one continuous sentence in each case; προσηγορικόν = common noun as opposed to a proper name (κύριον ὄνομα). Lower-case 'god' for Zeus and Amoun because Origen denies their divinity (ὁμολογῆσαι θεόν is a predicate, 'confess to be a god'). 'Forbid anyone to speak' renders the bare infinitive ὀνομάζειν after ἀπαγορεύουσιν; μόνῳ goes with θεῷ ('pray only to the God over all').
Pass A: the inline Greek lemma tags were moved out of the gloss into lemmas[] (the gloss was over a quarter Greek); the English gloss is unchanged.
